fatal_errors: The proposed material is pickled and passivated Q235 steel, whereas the target system is an initially uncoated SS316L substrate receiving an APS AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating and subsequent annealing.
The central intervention—approximately 150 µm atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi followed by 2 h annealing, especially at 550 °C—is entirely absent.

The cited Q235 evidence supports room-temperature cyclic atmospheric salt-spray corrosion only; it does not support extrapolation of the passivation-film mechanism to molten-salt exposure at 700–900 °C.
The proposed tests do not reproduce the target electrochemical medium or hot-corrosion conditions: 3.5 wt% H2SO4 and 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 mixtures are not specified.
No evidence supports the predicted high-temperature hardness response, brittle-rust behavior, or persistence of the initial nitrogen/fluorine-rich passivation film at hot-corrosion temperatures.
explanation: The answer presents an internally testable hypothesis for passivated Q235 and includes useful untreated and inert controls, time-resolved measurements, film-quality perturbation, and a falsification rule. The cited evidence validly supports passivation-film rupture, chloride-assisted corrosion, mixed-rust formation, and development followed by failure of a secondary protective rust layer during room-temperature atmospheric salt spray. However, it does not reconstruct the target material, HEA deposition, annealing treatment, phase/grain refinement, Al/Cr-rich passive oxides, or specified electrochemical and molten-salt exposures. Its high-temperature mechanism and outcomes are speculative extensions beyond the cited evidence. The generic concepts of barrier-film protection, chloride ingress, cracking, and eventual loss of continuity provide only weak mechanistic overlap with the target.
